subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram partial-stream finalization lacks clear delivery-mode observability (sent vs preview-finalized vs canceled)

question: Should this fix be limited to explicit Telegram final-delivery logs/events, or should it change the delivery confirmation boundary so session state is not treated as delivered until Telegram send/edit success is proven?
rationale: The issue asks for delivery-mode observability, while discussion and the linked PR move toward a stronger delivered-state boundary that affects fallback behavior and may require maintainer-owned semantics across channels.

options.title: Confirm delivery boundary
options.body: Require Telegram partial-stream finals to mark delivered only after all send/edit work succeeds, and expose the final mode for operators.

options.title: Limit to observability
options.body: Add explicit final-mode logs or events while preserving current session delivered-state behavior.

options.title: Defer to cross-channel design
options.body: Keep this issue open but make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561 decide the durable delivery contract first.

recommendation.title: Confirm delivery boundary
recommendation.body: Require Telegram partial-stream finals to mark delivered only after all send/edit work succeeds, and expose the final mode for operators.

likelyOwner.reason: The local history shows broad ownership across the Telegram delivery and plugin-boundary code involved in the product boundary decision.
